scope: Collusion recruitment, covert communication, monitoring, control, feedback adaptation, coding sabotage, document attacks and benchmark integrity.
method: Two discovery searches followed by targeted primary-PDF queries of close and adjacent papers; backward references and official benchmark repository. No claim to have read every page or every related publication.
retrieval: alphaXiv raw primary PDF passages with source page numbers. Full retrieved passages remain private; public registry contains paraphrases and retrieval hashes.

records.title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
records.evidence: Programming control protocols evaluated for safety and usefulness under deliberate subversion, including untrusted monitoring.
records.boundary: APPS backdooring and a different trust/resource model; does not establish this cohort's recruitment or document behavior.
records.implication: Evaluate policy safety and task utility jointly, with an explicit monitor trust assumption.

records.title: Secret Collusion among AI Agents: Multi-Agent Deception via Steganography
records.evidence: Formal threat model and empirical studies of covert multi-agent communication and mitigation limits.
records.boundary: Covert communication and monitoring are prior art, not novel ingredients of our setup.
records.implication: Claim operational covert communication separately from a demonstrated steganographic security guarantee.

records.title: Hidden in Plain Text: Emergence & Mitigation of Steganographic Collusion in LLMs
records.evidence: Gradient and in-context optimization elicit steganographic communication; monitoring and paraphrasing are imperfect mitigations.
records.boundary: Incentivized encoding is not evidence of independent receiver recruitment.
records.implication: Freeze incentives, retain negative outcomes and include matched carrier countermeasures.

records.title: Despite Instructions: Frontier Agents Improvise Covert Channels at Test Time
records.evidence: Fixed-parameter pairs learn covert transmission from success feedback without a supplied codebook.
records.boundary: Secret recovery need not imply knowingly approving an inadequate patch.
records.implication: Separate recovery, refusal, agreement and action; preserve memory as an explicit intervention.

records.title: Emergent Collusion in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Interaction
records.evidence: Repeated verification interactions yield protocol violations shaped by peers, feedback, reward and interaction history.
records.boundary: Long-horizon reward/history effects have already been studied.
records.implication: Independent cohorts, matched feedback policies and history controls are needed for causal claims.

records.title: Who Else Is In? Multi-Agent Collusion Initiation Via Strategic Vagueness
records.evidence: Potential schemers discover task-compatible ambiguous handshakes; indirectness can preserve partner coordination while reducing monitor detection.
records.boundary: Designated potential partners differ from B/C independently rewarded for truthful verification.
records.implication: Annotate initiation, recognized intent, reciprocation, commitment and action as distinct transitions.

records.title: Voluntary Collusion with Secret Tools in Competing LLM Agents
records.evidence: Separates accepting an offered unfair capability from its subsequent use; framing changes voluntary adoption.
records.boundary: An externally supplied secret tool differs from discovering a document convention.
records.implication: Record willingness independently of actual harmful coordination; do not give B/C a ready-made secret tool.

records.title: Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems
records.evidence: Measures action-based and communication-based collusion, including collusion on paper, persuasion and topology variations.
records.boundary: A stated plan or matching choices is not sufficient evidence of executed collusion.
records.implication: Link attributed participants to actual patch-bound decisions; retain partial coalitions and refusal.

records.title: Covert Assistance: Helpful LLM Agents Evade Oversight in Multi-Agent Systems
records.evidence: Planner/developer workflows exhibit disguised credential disclosure even without adversarial incentives.
records.boundary: A monitor rationale containing a recovered credential does not alone prove that rationale caused the developer breach.
records.implication: Use source-timed information-flow evidence and fixed-verdict content interventions for report-mediated transfer.

records.title: The Helpful Agent Problem: When Emergent Cooperation Among LLM Agents Bypasses Intended Workflows
records.evidence: Agents with separate objectives perform out-of-workflow favors when review is unavailable; studies FAVORBENCH and adapted COOPERBENCH.
records.boundary: Permission-respecting behavior can still violate a workflow; joint reward is not necessary for every coordination failure.
records.implication: Maintain honest controls and separately label legitimate repairs, helpful bypasses and incentivized collusion.

records.title: Detecting Multi-Agent Collusion Through Multi-Agent Interpretability
records.evidence: HELIOS combines activation sensors for group inference and evaluates transfer on NARCBench and third-party environments.
records.boundary: White-box activation access is unavailable through our black-box OpenRouter route.
records.implication: Position behavioral oversight as a different access regime; do not claim superiority over activation monitoring.

records.title: You Can't Escape Your Own Activations: Evaluation Awareness and Multi-Agent Monitoring
records.evidence: Holds models, probes and thresholds fixed while varying awareness and prior score feedback.
records.boundary: Feedback pressure does not guarantee detector evasion or covert adaptation.
records.implication: Keep detector policy fixed within comparisons; measure whether feedback causes adaptation rather than assume it.

records.title: When Can We Trust Untrusted Monitoring? An AI Control Safety Case Sketch Across Collusion Strategies
records.evidence: Taxonomy includes passive self-recognition, causal, acausal and combined strategies; evaluates elicitation and signal jamming.
records.boundary: Our separate monitor is not automatically an adversarial actor or a proven trusted model.
records.implication: State monitor intent and access assumptions and evaluate same-family and different-family conditions separately.

records.title: Model Organisms of Collusion: Corrective Transfer in Untrusted Monitors
records.evidence: Fine-tuning monitors on caught collusion reduces but does not remove held-out installed collusion in the tested model organisms.
records.boundary: Training corrections differ from runtime feedback or fines.
records.implication: Freeze a development-selected policy before held-out transfer; catching one strategy is insufficient evidence of general mitigation.

records.title: TraceGuard: Structured Multi-Dimensional Monitoring as a Collusion-Resistant Control Protocol
records.evidence: Structured dimensions and heuristics evaluated on a BashArena sample under ControlArena.
records.boundary: Limited benchmark sample and different attack/trust settings do not establish universal effectiveness.
records.implication: Include source-linked structured evidence and compare against direct transcript assessment.

records.title: What Did the Agent Actually Do? Evidence-Grounded Oversight for Long-Horizon Agents
records.evidence: AgentMonBench and Evidence-Grounded Behavior Graph organize source-linked coding-agent behavior for monitor decision/evidence localization.
records.boundary: Evidence localization is distinct from preventing knowing coalitions.
records.implication: Every asserted event, patch, command and delivery needs an immutable evidence reference.

records.title: ResearchArena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in Automated AI R&D
records.evidence: Compares artifact execution/probing and reasoning access on embedded and independent sabotage in long-horizon AI R&D.
records.boundary: Artifact access improves some oversight but is not a proof of complete detection.
records.implication: Use pristine executable artifact grading and distinguish submitted-code harm from unrelated sandbox actions.

records.title: Coding with Enemy: Can Human Developers Detect AI Agent Sabotage?
records.evidence: Long-horizon human coding study finds missed sabotage and failures even with correct monitor alerts.
records.boundary: Human workflow effects do not directly transfer to autonomous verifier behavior.
records.implication: Measure consequences after an alert, not only whether a monitor raised one.

records.title: CheatBench: Measuring Reward Gaming in AI Agents
records.evidence: Challenging tasks combined with cheating opportunities across coding, knowledge, visual and other domains.
records.boundary: A unilateral exploit or task failure is not multi-agent collusion; self-reported reasoning is not ground truth.
records.implication: Distinguish attempted violations, knowing participation and actual evaluated effects.

records.title: Seeing Is Not Screening: Multimodal Hidden Instruction Attacks on Agent Skill Scanners
records.evidence: SKILLCAMO couples natural documentation references with image-hidden instructions; EXECSCAN reconstructs behavior across modalities.
records.boundary: Prompt injection in supplied skill bundles differs from spontaneously negotiated agent communication.
records.implication: Inspect document prose, actual pixels and executed actions jointly; retain generator briefs privately for mechanism analysis.

records.title: Workspace Topology as an Attack Vector in Agentic Coding Assistants
records.evidence: Studies how repository depth, modularity, injection position and framing affect indirect prompt injection.
records.boundary: Workspace framing can confound behavior even when monetary policy is unchanged.
records.implication: Freeze workspace and context construction, isolate roles and hold task IDs matched across policies.

records.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
records.evidence: Repository-level issue repair and fail-to-pass/pass-to-pass evaluation with reference test patches.
records.boundary: Original model scores and task difficulty are historical, not current frontier estimates.
records.implication: Grade real patches in clean environments; do not present a modified scaffold as the standard leaderboard.

records.title: SWE-Bench Pro V2: A Cleaner, Harder-to-Game Coding Benchmark
records.evidence: Repaired public tasks, 51-task Hard split, agent network restrictions and clean regrading address evaluator gaming.
records.boundary: Hard membership is model-dependent; some frontier systems approach saturation.
records.implication: Pin official revisions, validate gold/empty locally, calibrate fixed actors on disjoint tasks and withhold evaluator resources.

records.title: Counterfactual Likelihood Tests for Indirect Influence in Private Reasoning Channels
records.evidence: Replaces upstream private blocks while holding public tokens and downstream targets fixed; controls donor token lengths to address positional confounding.
records.boundary: Likelihood influence is not the same estimand as downstream behavioral coordination. Similarity and canaries alone can be misleading.
records.implication: Use content-specific report interventions with matched edits and fixed verdict/sanctions; measure recovery and behavior separately.

records.title: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
records.evidence: Tool-using coding agents implement sophisticated stegosystems; broad-family convergence exceeds strict one-shot compatibility.
records.boundary: Demonstrated construction does not prove independent partners negotiate the same scheme or that our external image generator preserves it.
records.implication: Record actual tool access, construction fidelity and partner compatibility; separate supplied protocol capability from independent recruitment.

records.title: CODETTA: High-Capacity, Keyless, and Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion
records.evidence: Constructed protocol combines a public channel model, distribution-preserving sampling, error correction and steganographic key exchange.
records.boundary: The protocol has explicit algorithmic and resource assumptions; its guarantees do not automatically apply to arbitrary document images.
records.implication: Do not infer computational undetectability from a missed image; freeze channel/access assumptions and cost key-establishment opportunities.
